name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: a slipping group share, a mixed October and the parts marked mid-bracket
frontmatter.summary: October was a mix shift inside a falling share: Toyota rose 7.7% to 23,551 while Daihatsu fell -6.8% to 10,772, the two about two fifths of a market up 2.4%, and the company's nine-month 49.0% reconciles to above fifty per cent a year earlier. BYD's third place is wholesale; its retail fell to 6,355, barely above Suzuki's 6,284. The auto mark moved to its bracket midpoint: HOLD at Rp4,694.
thesis: The group share is slipping, not holding: the nine-month 49.0% is about three and a half points below the level the company's own growth rates imply for the prior year, and the visible October table — Toyota 23,551, Daihatsu 10,772 and Isuzu 3,119 of 81,482 — is about forty-six per cent [S14, S31, S33, F57, F125, F179, F102].

The month itself is a mix shift: Toyota gained 7.7% and Daihatsu gave up -6.8%, leaving the two brands flat at a little over two fifths of a market up 2.4%; BYD's 6,639 wholesale is dealer stocking, with retail down to 6,355, only a hair above Suzuki's 6,284 [S31, S33, S20, F166, F180, F182].

The parts are worth Rp4,392 after the 35% discount, with the automotive block at the midpoint of its sourced multiple bracket rather than its top; un-rolled, the parts plus the Rp399 dividend sit below the Rp5,000 price, and the roll takes the expected return to 1.9% [S0, S15, S25, S32, cov_publish comps].

The financing block is on its annualised actual return, the unlisted blocks at sourced floors, and parent G&A is already inside the segment incomes; the tails are discount-path probabilities, with the operating breaks quantified in the text [S14, S15, S5, F78]

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and ongoing with no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14].

blocks.text: **What changed.** Two corrections and one mark. First, the share statement [S31, S33, S14]: the company's 49.0% nine-month measure, set against its own 13.0% sales growth in a market up a fifth, implies a prior-year share above fifty-two per cent, so the trend is about minus three and a half points, not the minus two the draft implied; the visible October table — Toyota 23,551, Daihatsu 10,772 and Isuzu 3,119 of 81,482 — is about forty-six per cent [S14, S31, S33, F57, F125, F179, F102]. The prior draft's "stable share" reading is withdrawn, and so is its use of the fifty-one per cent reachable-share statement as a prior-year actual [S4, F14]. Second, the retail series: BYD's third place is wholesale, and its retail fell to 6,355 from 7,421, only a hair above Suzuki's 6,284 [S33, F180, F181, F182] — the strongest evidence the displacement is thinner than the table reads. Third, the automotive block is now marked at the midpoint of its sourced bracket rather than the top, taking the parts to Rp4,392 and the target to Rp4,694; no forecast input moves [S25, S32, S15].

**The call stands, on a thinner cushion.** Target Rp4,694 against Rp5,000, an expected total return of 1.9% including Rp399 of dividends: **HOLD**. Un-rolled, Rp4,458 plus the dividend is below the price; the one-year roll at the 14.6% cost of equity is what makes the return positive, a convention and not a thesis. Base Rp4,712 at 45%, bear Rp4,388 at 30%, bull Rp5,032 at 25%; with the four-hundred-and-twenty-rupiah operating break inside the bear at that weight — a figure the engine cannot write into a holding — the weighted value is about four thousand five hundred and seventy and the return about minus zero point six per cent; the rating holds (Section five).

**Variant view.** The price capitalises the parts at a 26.0% discount, near the narrow end of the card's range, and we hold 35% — the name's own level, one step below the median — because there is no dated narrowing catalyst and related-party purchases are IDR84.94tn [S8, S14, S16, S6, cov_publish comps]. The peer set is an anchor, not a validation: Astra's own row sits inside it and no five-year own-discount series exists (Section four).

Astra is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates across vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property, reporting Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as core businesses [S2, S3]. FY2025 parent net income split Automotive IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, heavy equipment and mining IDR9.10tn, agribusiness IDR1.17tn, infrastructure IDR1.26tn, IT IDR0.21tn and property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The Others column is material: nine-month attributable profit was IDR2.56tn, up more than a third [S14]. Jardine Cycle & Carriage controls 50.1% on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0]. The parent is itself an operating distributor, not a passive holdco [S6].

National wholesales reached 760,476 units over ten months and 81,482 in October, 31.2% on a weak October 2025 base and 2.4% on September; retail reached 758,653 and 82,429, 29.3% and 1.5% [S20]. One source conflict, noted: Inilah puts the October year-on-year rise at about ten per cent, but the same article's units against GAIKINDO's 62,090 October 2025 base give 31.2%, and we use the GAIKINDO series [S20, S33, F104]. At October's pace the year lands just below the top of the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range, above the industry body's target [S20, S9, F138].

**The share is slipping; October was a mix shift inside it.** One denominator, one table. GAIKINDO's October brand data give units for Toyota, Daihatsu and Isuzu, the three Astra-distributed marques that appear in the published top ten [S31, S33]; UD Trucks and Peugeot are not in the table and no registered source gives a unit figure for either, so the visible share is a floor.

| Marque (Astra-distributed) | Oct 2026 wholesale | Sep 2026 wholesale | Basis of the Astra link | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Toyota | 23,551 | 21,875 | distribution franchise, consolidated [S6] | | Daihatsu | 10,772 | 11,558 | Astra-Daihatsu joint venture [S6, S14] | | Isuzu | 3,119 | not published | PT Isuzu Astra Motor Indonesia, an associate [S6] | | National market | 81,482 | 79,538 | GAIKINDO wholesales [S31, S33] |

Toyota and Daihatsu together, 23,551 and 10,772, were about two fifths of the market, flat on September's 21,875 and 11,558 in 79,538 [S31]; adding Isuzu's 3,119 takes the visible group total to about forty-six per cent, below the company's 49.0% nine-month "pangsa pasar Astra secara keseluruhan" [S31, S33, F179]. The two reconcile only if the nine-month measure includes marques outside the top ten, which is why the trend, not the level, is the honest test: 13.0% sales growth against a market up a fifth [S14] implies a prior-year share above fifty-two per cent, so the nine-month measure is about minus three and a half points year on year. October's two-brand share was nonetheless flat on September, so the month itself is a mix shift, not a break [S31, S20, F166].

**BYD's third place is a wholesale ranking, and the retail disagrees.** BYD's 6,639 wholesale put it third, ahead of Suzuki's 6,104 and Honda's 3,478 [S31, S33]; but its retail fell to 6,355 from 7,421, and Suzuki's rose to 6,284 — a gap of a few dozen units, not a displacement [S33, F180, F181, F182]. The wholesale-retail gap is dealer stocking, consistent with October's national retail of 82,429 exceeding wholesale [S20, S33]. We test the bear's China premise on retail and size the cohort on wholesale: BYD and Jaecoo alone were 6,639 and 3,514, together about an eighth of the 81,482 market, with Chery's 640 and Geely's 1,560 taking the cohort to about fifteen per cent [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185]. That cohort sits above the LCGC price point where Daihatsu's 10,772 live, so the direct overlap is at the margin; the LCGC channel's own -11.0% decline is the larger Daihatsu fact [S18, F91, F92].

**The restock arithmetic, once.** Ten-month 2025 retail of 585,926 exceeded wholesale of 561,405; nine-month 2026 wholesale of 679,020 exceeded retail of 676,000; October retail then exceeded wholesale by 947 units, unwinding them — a real but residual fourth-quarter risk [S20, S26, F26, F112, F124, F106, F143].

**LCGC is the structural channel, and the group's exposure is Daihatsu.** LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in nine months, -11.0%, about one car in eight of 679,020, against one in six a year earlier [S18]. Daihatsu was 10,772 of the 81,482 October market, and its retail was 121,471 over ten months, 8.0% [S31, S28]. The trade-up volume is captured by the Toyota franchise Astra also distributes, so the split is margin-relevant but not obviously margin-negative [S31, S18].

**Motorcycles: two measures, and we use the company's.** The company reports national wholesales up 4.0% to 5,000,000; Adira Finance, outside the group, reports retail of 5,100,000, up 10.0% [S14, S26]. They differ in measure, not direction, and Adira is a peer read-across, never a consolidated subsidiary or a mark.

**Position and moat.** Toyota and Daihatsu lead cars and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles; the distribution and financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes shape demand [S14, S9]; the house deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, held back by the Martabe outage and the coal quota; the third quarter ran at a better margin as mining recovered [S15, S14]. Selling and administrative expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, of which IDR2.96tn was non-recurring; clean net profit was IDR24.57tn [S15, S14].

Three basis corrections: the 30 September accounts are unaudited ("tidak diaudit"), so their gearing and book figures are interim [S15, S6]; capex is the audited expenses-by-nature line of IDR18.46tn, restating the data pack's smaller figure [S6, F111, S0]; depreciation is restated from the notes at IDR17.87tn for FY2025 and IDR16.70tn for FY2024, giving FY2025 EBITDA of IDR56,536.0bn at a margin of 17.5% [S6].

**Actual versus forecast, on one basis.** FY2026E net profit of IDR33,015.0bn is the clean nine months of IDR24.57tn plus an implied fourth quarter of about eight and a half trillion rupiah, roughly flat on the fourth quarter of 2025 — FY2025 profit of IDR32,769.0bn less the nine-month comparative of IDR24.47tn — the ordinary seasonal step down [S14, F149]. Other income of IDR11,548.0bn is the clean nine-month figure annualised, so the charge is excluded rather than added back [S15, F48]. The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 16.1% sits below FY2025A because it is the nine-month actual: flat revenue with a cost ratio just over eleven per cent, carried at 11.1% against the audited 10.1%, then gliding down as costs grow with the deck's inflation against 5.0% nominal revenue growth [S15, S6, KB macro deck]. No cost-cut programme or LCGC-mix benefit is assumed; the minority take is held at 11.0%, above the reported nine-month IDR2.47tn of minorities' interest in IDR24.07tn of consolidated profit, rather than stepping up to the audited mix [S15, S0, F170, F171].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are clean: operating cash flow of IDR28.61tn over nine months exceeded profit [S15]. Non-recurring items are optics-class and stripped before the sum of the parts [S14]. Astra's own provision stock is IDR3.07tn current and IDR2.41tn non-current at 30 June, flat on the year-end while current receivables rose to IDR52.54tn, so coverage eased slightly; the first-half charge of IDR1.16tn is already inside the nine-month income [S5]. Adira Finance is a peer read-across only: gross NPF 1.8%, provision expense down 10.0% [S26]. Related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn were about a third of cost and sales IDR27.94tn under a tenth of revenue, with no transfer-pricing test possible on consolidated accounts; revaluation was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted placement was found [S6].
A holding company with listed and unlisted parts: the sum of the parts carries 96% of the weight, cross-checked by earnings and book at 2% and 2% [S0].

The table carries the build — risk-free 7.4% less sovereign spread 1.6%, levered beta 1.32 on debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.59, mature-market premium and country risk — to a cost of equity of 14.6% and WACC of 11.9% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

**The parts.** The automotive block is the nine-month actual of IDR9.79tn annualised at four thirds, not October's higher 81,482, marked at the midpoint of the only two sourced, dated multiples on this income: Selamat Sempurna's Rp1,640 close on 6 November over audited FY2025 earnings per share of Rp195 at the top — the IDR1.12tn of audited profit over 5,758,675,440 shares [S25, S32, F172, F173, F174, F175] — and Astra Otoparts' forward six and a half times at the bottom. Both are components businesses on a Toyota/Daihatsu distribution plus AHM motorcycle base and no listed Indonesian distribution or motorcycle comparable exists; the prior draft carried the top, which is why the mark falls [S25, S32, cov_publish comps]. One convention only, on annualised income. The bracket spans about twenty-four trillion rupiah of gross value, roughly four hundred rupiah per share after the discount and about three hundred and eighty of target — HOLD at both ends [S25, S32, F68, F173]. The listed stakes are at the 6 November close: United Tractors Rp23,025 on 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari Rp9,450 on 79.7% and Astra Graphia Rp2,500 on 76.9% [S21, S22, S23, S6]. The financing block is book/ROE: income includes joint-venture results, so the book includes JV investments of IDR9.28tn against liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]; at the 14.6% cost of equity the justified P/B is about one and a fifth times book on the annualised actual, which carries the first-half charge [S0, S15].

Infrastructure: the IDR22.68tn is the Others-column equity-method book; Astra Tol Nusantara is consolidated (IDR24.85tn of assets) and not inside it; its directly held concession rights are a separate intangible at IDR9.37tn, additive and at book [S15, F123, F122, F146]. Serasi Autoraya is already inside the automotive mark [S15, F145]. The Others column is a floor: assets of IDR76.73tn against liabilities of IDR18.64tn leave about fifty-eight trillion rupiah of book equity against those two marks, the gap mostly the property markdown [S15, F161, F162, S27].

Property is marked on MMLP's Rp214 close, which capitalises its IDR6.48tn of assets below book, applied to Menara Astra's IDR26.48tn [S27, F119, F120, F121]. Two limitations: MMLP is a warehouse/logistics owner and Menara is CBD office plus warehouses, and no Jakarta CBD cap rate or appraised office value exists in any registered source, so the transfer is disclosed; and the markdown is large — twenty trillion rupiah of Menara assets carried at four and a half trillion leaves about fifteen trillion outside the marks, roughly two hundred and fifty rupiah per share after the discount. With the Others reconciliation, about twenty trillion of book equity is outside the marks: a floor, not a valuation [S15, S27, S6].

**Parent G&A is not a separate deduction.** The parent is an operating distributor whose revenue of IDR96.19tn, gross profit of IDR9.64tn and profit of IDR19.89tn are consolidated, its G&A of IDR4.52tn already inside the segment income the automotive block is marked on; capitalising it at ten times would deduct about forty-five trillion twice [S6, F78, F96, F97, F98].

The cross-checks — P/E Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, 23.5% and 52.2% above the parts — are undiscounted while the parts carry a 35% discount, P/BV uses the 30 September book of IDR238.10tn, and the averages were struck when mining earned far more (H1-2025 profit IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn) [S0, S15, S5]. The bridge carries no buyback line: retirement cuts the share count and the cash spent is out of the parent cash of IDR2.64tn it deducts [S15, S14, F80]. Its consolidated net-debt line is the data-pack figure, labelled as such and below the filed IDR64.92tn; no method applies it, since the parts deduct parent short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against that cash plus leases of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S0, S15, F100, F81, F84, F85].

**The discount is the base rate; the peer set is an anchor, not a validation.** The base holds 35%, the name's own level, one step below the exact two-fifths median [cov_publish comps]. Corrected against the table: only two names sit at thirty per cent, BRPT and CUAN; ADRO is at twenty-three per cent; IMJS is the sixty, ITMA the seventy-four; PACK is twenty-five and BNBR thirty-eight. The median excluding Astra's own row is still forty per cent, which is why the bear carries it — but Astra's own row is inside the set, so the match is circular, and no five-year own-discount series exists, so the card's own-history test cannot be run; the closest own series is the FY2025 P/B of 0.9x [S0, S15, cov_publish comps]. On the rolled table a five-point widening to the median turns the return negative, the base is 1.9%, and a five-point narrowing lifts it to high single digits [S0]. Two facts argue against narrowing below the name's own level: the undated buyback [S8, S14, S16] and related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn [S6]. Upstream cover is above one — parent profit IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22].

**Target and roll.** The base compounds Rp4,458 at the 14.6% cost of equity and nets Rp399 of dividends, giving Rp4,712; weighting base 45%, bear 30% at Rp4,388 and bull 25% at Rp5,032 gives Rp4,694 [S15, S0]. The red team is right that the roll does the work: un-rolled, Rp4,458 plus Rp399 is below the Rp5,000 price, about minus three per cent, and the one-year roll at 14.6% is what turns 1.9% positive — a convention, not a thesis, and why the call is a hold and not an add. The per-share count is the 30 September figure of just under forty billion shares, pre-buyback: the cash is deducted through parent net debt and the retirement is not credited, so each retirement at this discount would add value the base does not carry [S15, S0]. The target and this return EXCLUDE the operating break quantified in Section five, and the exclusion is structural rather than a judgement: the holdco_sotp engine holds every listed stake at the 6 November close and reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so a break inside a stake has no engine line [S15, S0]. Priced at its 30% weight that break takes the weighted value to about four thousand five hundred and seventy and the expected return to about minus zero point six per cent, which is still HOLD; the rating would need worse than minus ten per cent to move.

**What the price implies.** At Rp5,000 the parts are capitalised at a 26.0% discount, narrower than the 35% we carry. That gap is the call: on the market's rate the target sits below the price and the return is the dividend carry, 1.9% against -6.1%, because nothing dates the narrowing [S0, cov_publish comps]. The FY2025 P/B of 0.9x and a price below the 30 September book are a cheapness signal, not a catalyst [S0, S15].

**The engine's limit, labelled.** The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every case, so the shocks do not reprice the parts; the tabulated bear and bull are discount-path values [S15, S14].

**The bear's operating breaks, from the reconciled level.** Share goes first: the two points come off the visible October level of about forty-six per cent, not off 49.0%, because the month already sits below the nine-month measure — BYD and Jaecoo alone took about an eighth of the market, and the Chinese cohort is about fifteen per cent once Chery and Geely are counted [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185, F179, F102]; two points is about sixty-four rupiah per share at the midpoint mark [S14, F125]. Then a reversal of the restocking swing, roughly one unit in twenty-eight of nine-month wholesale [S20, F26, F112, F143]; a credit break, a repeat of the first-half charge taking the financing mark to book, about a sixth of the block or one hundred and ninety rupiah per share [S5, F35, F167, F168]; and the currency break — related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn are largely dollar-linked, so a five-to-ten per cent rupiah move is a twentieth to a tenth of that flow, one and a half to three and a half per cent of nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn and two fifths to seven eighths of automotive nine-month income of IDR9.79tn with no pass-through [S6, S15, F21, F41, F68], while the disclosed monetary sensitivity is IDR0.95tn of profit, a floor [S6, F165]. The four breaks sum to about four hundred and twenty rupiah per share at their midpoints — roughly one and a third times the three hundred and twenty-four rupiah base-to-bear gap the table itself shows — so the tabulated bear at Rp4,388 understates the operating downside by that amount [S15, S5, F35, F167, F168]. We use one figure throughout, here and in the bear note: four hundred and twenty.

**Daihatsu and LCGC, quantified.** Inside an LCGC channel that ran 83,997 units over nine months, -11.0% year on year [S18, F91, F92], Daihatsu's October share was 10,772 of 81,482, down -6.8% on the month [S31, F154, F156]; if it halved, the block would lose roughly a sixteenth of its volume — the second-largest break [S31, S18, F68].

**The rating does not depend on the weights — but it does lean on the dividend.** Price the operating break inside the bear — Rp4,388 less the four hundred and twenty rupiah quantified above — and the probability-weighted value is about four thousand five hundred and seventy against the published target of Rp4,694, an expected return of about minus zero point six per cent instead of 1.9%, with the un-rolled return at about minus five per cent [S0, S15]. That is the all-in figure; the published target and return exclude the break because the engine holds each listed stake at the 6 November close and cannot reprice a mark inside a holding [S15, S0]. Doubling the bear weight to three fifths of the mix takes the all-in value to about four thousand three hundred and forty-five and the return to about minus five per cent, still inside the HOLD band. The forty per cent peer median on its own returns about minus four per cent, still inside the HOLD band; REDUCE needs worse than minus ten per cent, reached only at the card's outer edge [S0, S15]. So the honest statement is: HOLD, and the cushion is the dividend and the discount, not the marks.
**Regulatory and commodity — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and subsidies shape the car market; coal, gold, nickel and palm oil run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency — medium likelihood, material impact.** The desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and is cautious on rate-sensitive demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on demand and credit, and that caution sits in the country risk premium [S2, S4].

**Competitive and technology — high likelihood, material impact.** Chinese and electrified entrants threaten the franchise, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; the nine-month measure has moved to 49.0% from about fifty-two per cent implied a year earlier, so this is a trend, not a tail [S9, S14, F57, F125].

**Credit and provisioning — medium likelihood, material impact.** IDR66.70tn of net debt against receivables of IDR132.00tn; Astra's own provision stock is flat and coverage eased as the book grew, so the risk is a break in that stability; the Adira read-across outside the group is not evidence on Astra's book [S5, S14, S26, F35, F167, F168].

**Governance, control and liquidity — high structural impact, low liquidity risk.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. Liquidity is not a constraint: turnover is IDR244.7bn a day and parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend [S0, S6, S10].

The base (45%) carries the actual nine months annualised, the ordinary seasonal fourth quarter, the nine-month cost ratio gliding to the audited ratio, the minority mix held, and the discount at 35% with no narrowing [S14, S20]. The bull (25%) has share recovering toward the company's stated 51.0% reachable level, the coal quota resetting, costs holding at the nine-month ratio, and the discount narrowing five points to thirty per cent [S14, S11, S18, cov_publish comps]. The bear (30%) is the mirror on the discount — five points wider, to the peer median — with the operating breaks in the text, not the engine target [S14, S5, S9]. The shocks are mirrored; the probabilities are not, because the narrowing catalyst is undated and the share trend is negative.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Buyback execution at the completed pace, a dated capital-allocation event that upstreams cash, the November brand split showing Daihatsu stabilising while Toyota holds share, retail keeping pace with wholesale so the restocking swing unwinds without a volume cut, and Astra's own provision coverage holding at the June level [S14, S20, S5].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S0, S6]; no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed [S6]. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026 and the IDR8.00tn programme approved in July runs with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95 per cent lifts the stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November, so it is a small transfer from parent to minorities [S19]. ESG exposures are coal, palm oil, nickel and the vehicle transition, met through Japanese partners rather than a platform the group owns [S14, S9].

**Audit, listing status and related-party gravity.** The FY2025 accounts carry no readable audit opinion — the report pages are blank and no auditor is named — so we record that rather than an audited-clean opinion [S6]. No source states the IDX board or a special notation; we found no special-monitoring disclosure or notation letter — an absence of evidence, not a clean bill [S6, S15]. Purchases of IDR84.94tn were about a sixth of total assets of IDR507.37tn and sales of IDR27.94tn about a twentieth [S6, F20, F21, F148]. These are optics-class structural flags, not confirmed manipulation: disclosed, and principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures, but the purchase flow is large enough to widen the warranted discount [S6, F21].

The dated catalysts are the Otoparts tender close, the monthly wholesale data and the FY2026 audited results, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S13, S20, S4]. None is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst: the base holds the base-rate discount and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

We monitor the ten-month run-rate of 760,476 and Astra's monthly share, last stated at about 50.0% through August [S20, S30, F57]; the monthly brand split, Toyota 23,551 against Daihatsu 10,772 and BYD at 6,639 ahead of Suzuki 6,104 and Honda 3,478 [S31, S33]; Daihatsu's retail pace [S28]; the wholesale-retail gap [S20, F26, F112]; the LCGC versus up-class split [S18]; Komatsu units and overburden [S14]; financing receivables and Astra's own provisioning [S14, S5]; buyback execution [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid [S6].

bear.narrative: Four operating breaks, each with its measured size, and a discount back to the peer median. (1) AUTO SHARE AND MIX: the company's own nine-month share is 49.0%, and its own growth rates reconcile it to about 52.5% for the prior-year nine months - Astra sales up 13% against a national market up 21% [S14, F57, F125] - so the trend is broadly minus three and a half points, not minus two; the visible October table, Toyota 23,551 plus Daihatsu 10,772 plus Isuzu 3,119 of 81,482, is about 45.9% [S31, S33, F151, F154, F179, F102], so we start the further loss from that reconciled level rather than from 49%. A further two-point loss to the Chinese cohort - BYD plus Jaecoo alone were 10,153 units, 12.5% of the October market, with Chery and Geely adding 2,200 more [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185] - is about 4% of the block's volume, which at the 7.475x annualised multiple the block is marked on (Selamat Sempurna's FY2025 price-earnings multiple at the 6 November close, applied to annualised nine-month income [S32, S25, F68]) is roughly Rp3.9tn of gross value before the 35% discount, about Rp64 per share. (2) RESTOCK REVERSAL: nine-month wholesale of 679,020 now exceeds retail of 676,000, after retail exceeded wholesale by 24,521 units a year earlier (F124 retail of 585,926 less F106 wholesale of 561,405, both ten-month 2025) [S14, S20, F26, F112, F124, F106] - about 24,400 units, 3.6% of nine-month wholesale, is dealer restocking rather than end demand, and a retail-led fourth quarter gives it back. (3) MINING: the base carries mining at the nine-month actual run-rate, not a normalised recovery, so the bear item is a further fall from that run-rate rather than a non-recovery: the national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. (4) CREDIT: Astra's own financing book was stable, not improving - provision stock essentially flat at Rp3,069bn current and Rp2,408bn non-current against current receivables up to Rp52,541bn, so coverage eased as the book grew [S5, F167, F168, F169], with the Rp1,160bn H1 charge already inside the nine-month income [S5, F35]; Adira Finance is outside the group and is a peer read-across only, not evidence on Astra's book [S26] - so the bear is a break from that stability, not its continuation: a repeat of the Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge inside one quarter against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60] takes the block's return to about the cost of equity and the mark from 1.21x to 1.0x book, about Rp10.8tn or a sixth of the block. (5) CURRENCY: related-party purchases of Rp84,937bn are largely dollar-linked [S6, F21], so a 5-10% rupiah move is a twentieth to a tenth of that flow, 1.5-3.5% of nine-month revenue [S15, F41] and two fifths to seven eighths of automotive nine-month income [S14, F68] if none is passed through; the company's disclosed monetary sensitivity is Rp948bn of profit [S6, F165], a floor rather than the full exposure. The buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the ~40% peer median, from the 35% base [S8, S14], a mirrored 5pp move. Disclosed limit: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so the table carries the discount and the earnings weight only; the four operating breaks above are quantified here and in section 5, not in the tabulated bear. Their total is about Rp420 per share, roughly one and a third times the Rp324 base-to-bear gap the table shows, and is not used to justify the bear's 30% weight. We state plainly that the published bear therefore UNDERSTATES the operating downside by about Rp420 per share beyond the tabulated discount path: UNTR is 18% of gross value and is held at the 6 November close in every case, so the named mining non-recovery has zero value effect in the table. The exclusion is structural, not a judgement: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so a break inside a stake has no engine line [S15, S0]; section 5 therefore prices the same Rp420 at the bear's 30 per cent weight outside the table and gives the target and the return including it (about Rp4,568 and about minus 0.6 per cent) [S0, S15].

bull.narrative: Three operating breaks and a mirrored discount. (1) AUTO SHARE: ten-month wholesales reached 760,476 units and October ran at 81,482 [S20, F101, F102], and the bull's incremental assumption is that Astra's 49% share recovers toward the level its own growth rates imply for the prior-year nine months, about 52% [S14, F57, F125], rather than that the market beats its range, with Astra taking the up-class volume it is already selling [S18]; two points of share back at the 7.475x annualised multiple the block is marked on (9.9667x on the nine-month fact) [S32, S25] adds roughly the Rp3.9tn the bear removes, the mirrored move. (2) MINING: the national coal quota resets and the complex stabilises - a bull assumption, not in the base - with the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap [S11]. (3) COST AND MIX: share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin and the opex ratio holds at the third quarter's 10.84% instead of gliding to the audited 10.14% [S15, S6]. (4) DISCOUNT: the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the 35% base to 30%, Astra's 30% bottom of the peer cohort - we do not assume a break below it without a dated catalyst, and the undated buyback is not one [S8, S14, S16]. The bull narrows the discount by 5pp, the mirror of the bear. The Others/infrastructure run-rate is NOT a bull-only item: the base marks that block at the 30 September book, which already carries the nine-month Others profit of Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S14, F71]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) sits outside the table because it is a transfer inside an already consolidated block. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue. From FY2027E the ratio glides from the third quarter's 10.84% actual to the FY2025 audited 10.14% [S6]: the nine-month 11.22% is depressed by the Martabe outage, which cut revenue (the same base effect the 21.3% nine-month gross margin shows), and the third quarter - after the gold restart and the coal-volume recovery - already ran at 10.84% [S15, S14]. Holding 11.22% to FY2035 would mean costs growing at revenue growth in perpetuity, a permanent step-up of about Rp3.2tn a year of EBIT against the audited ratio, which is an unsourced conservative drift, not the last actual. The glide is mechanical, not a forecast: costs grow with the macro deck's inflation (3.28%) against 5% nominal revenue [KB macro deck], a ratio factor of 0.984 a year, so the ratio falls from 10.84% to 10.66%, 10.49% and 10.32% over FY2028E-FY2030E and converges to the audited 10.14% in the long run. Real cost per unit of revenue is therefore held at the last actual, which is what the base-case card asks for.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual from the expenses-by-nature note, capex Rp18,464bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn, or 5.71% [S6, F111]; the data pack's Rp17,440bn is a different capex definition and is not used now that the audited line is sourced. The group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised further.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. The reported nine-month take is 10.3% (Rp2,471bn on Rp24,073bn [S15, F170, F171]), so 11% is a deliberate fourth quarter at the third quarter's 15.5% take, 0.7pp above the reported actual and 1.9pp above the clean 9.1%. From FY2027E the take is held at that same 11% full-year rate, not the clean nine-month 9.1%, because the base carries the nine-month revenue, margin and cost ratios forward and does not add a mining recovery: a step to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]) would require the segment-mix shift the base does not forecast and would cut parent profit by about 7% on an unsourced basis. The mining-recovery sensitivity sits in the bull shock on revenue, margin and share count, where it belongs, rather than in the base through the minority ratio [S15, S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -4.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] is carried to completion at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65], which is about Rp0.9tn a month. Rp8tn at that pace retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, in roughly nine months, inside FY2027E. The prior 2.0% truncated the programme after one year for no sourced reason and understated the only holdco-level capital return the company is actually executing; the remaining uncertainty is timing, not the pace, and the bull carries no extra retirement.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 35%, which is Astra's own level in the house CONGLOMERATES peer set and sits BELOW the peer median of 40%: the 14-name set shows ASII at 0.35, a median of exactly 0.40, only TWO names at 0.30 (BRPT and CUAN), ADRO at 0.2311, BNBR at 0.38, BHIT at 0.40, IMJS at 0.60, ITMA at 0.741, PACK at 0.25 and ZBRA at 0.6625; the median excluding ASII's own row is also 0.40, and no JKON or TSPC entry exists in the set [cov_publish comps]. The set is an ANCHOR, not a validation: ASII's own 0.35 sits inside it, so reading the match as corroboration is circular (red team C41, accepted), and no ASII five-year observed discount series exists in the data pack, so VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 2's own-history test cannot be run and is disclosed rather than faked - the closest own series is the FY2025 P/B of 0.9x [S0]. The 35% is therefore not a midpoint between the name's own level and the median - there is no 30% own level and no 35% JKON reference - it is the name's own level, one step below the median, and it is capped there by the two name-specific facts that argue for a wider discount than the 0.30 cohort: there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM carries no end date or disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16]) and related-party purchases were Rp84.9tn, about 30% of cost of revenue plus SGA, a structural and untested flow that the method card says widens the warranted discount [S6, F21]. We do not import the 40% median of small, illiquid names into a blue-chip whose NAV is mostly listed and marked at market. Upstream cover is above one on the parent's accounts - FY2025 profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22] - so the discount is not argued from dividend distress. The discount is independent of the share price: the target is an output of the marks and this discount, not a reproduction of the 6 November close [S0]. The published bear carries the 40% peer median and the bull the 30% bottom of the cohort; the rating at 25/30/35/40/45% is shown in section 4. At 40% the target gives an expected total return of about minus 8%, still inside the HOLD band; REDUCE needs worse than minus 10%, reached only near 45%. The prior draft's claim that the call turns REDUCE at the peer median was wrong.

challenges.challenge: The group-share evidence does not reconcile. Toyota+Daihatsu = 34,323 of 81,482 = 42.1%, but the report calls that a lower bound of the 49% nine-month company measure, whose own source says only 'pangsa pasar Astra secara keseluruhan' (S14) and does not define the marques. Adding Isuzu 3,119 (PT Isuzu Astra Motor Indonesia, a group JV in S6) gives 37,442/81,482 = 45.9%, not 49%. Separately, 51% in FY2025 with Astra sales +13% against a market +21% (S14) implies 47.6%, not 49.0%, so at least one of 51%, 49% and the two growth rates is on a different base.
challenges.answer: Accepted: one-denominator marque table added for Oct and Sep and the 49% measure defined as the company all-marque nine-month figure; held-its-share withdrawn, trend restated at about minus 3.5pp on the company own +13% against +21% inputs [S14, S31, S33].

challenges.challenge: S33 - the source the draft now registers and cites - reports that BYD's October retail FELL about 14% m/m, from 7,421 to 6,355, only 71 units above Suzuki's retail 6,284; its third place on wholesales is dealer stocking, not consumer displacement, and S33's own sub-head reads 'BYD Naik, Tapi Ritelnya Turun'. The draft cites S33 only for the ranking and reads the position as structural pressure ('consistent rather than a one-month spike') without the retail reversal, which is the strongest available argument that the competitive threat is overstated.
challenges.answer: Accepted: retail series cited - BYD retail 6,355 from 7,421, only 71 units above Suzuki 6,284 - and the bear China premise now tested on retail, with the wholesale-retail gap read as dealer stocking [S33, S20].

challenges.challenge: The China cohort is not sized. S33's table has Jaecoo eighth at 3,514, so BYD+Jaecoo are 10,153 units, 12.5% of the 81,482 October market; EV wholesales were 101,171 in eight months against 50,749 (+99%) [S9, F93/F94]; LCGC wholesales are -11% while the market is +21% [S18]. The bear adds 'a further two-point loss' from a 49% base that the October data already put below 46% on the visible table.
challenges.answer: Accepted: cohort sized - BYD 6,639 plus Jaecoo 3,514 is 12.5% of October, 15.2% with Chery and Geely - and the bear two-point loss starts from the reconciled October 45.9%, not from 49% [S31, S33, S18].

challenges.challenge: The auto block (109,576, 38.7% of the 283,008 gross value) is marked at 8.40x - the top of the analyst's own disclosed 6.55x-8.40x bracket - on Selamat Sempurna, a components exporter, applied to a mixed Toyota/Daihatsu distribution plus AHM motorcycle base. The prior review objected to the blanket mean; the response replaced the 7.36x mean with 8.40x, raising the mark. At 6.55x the block is 85,471: -24,103 gross, about -Rp395/share after the discount and about -Rp379 of target (still HOLD).
challenges.answer: Accepted: auto block marked at the bracket midpoint 7.475x annualised (9.9667x on the nine-month fact), not the 8.40x top; both bounds are components peers and no distribution or motorcycle comparable exists; target shown at both ends, HOLD across [S25, S32, F68].

challenges.challenge: The discount paragraph's comp description is wrong against the table it cites: cov_publish comps shows ADRO at 0.2311, not 0.30; ITMA at 0.741, with 0.60 belonging to IMJS; only BRPT and CUAN sit at 0.30, not 'three names'; and ASII's own 0.35 in that set is the assumption under test, so the corroboration is circular. The 0.40 median is right, but the bear's 40% and bull's 30% are described against a misread set, and no ASII own five-year observed discount series is shown.
challenges.answer: Accepted: figures corrected - ADRO 0.2311, only BRPT and CUAN at 0.30, IMJS 0.60, ITMA 0.741, PACK 0.25, BNBR 0.38; ASII own 0.35 sits inside the set so the corroboration is circular and no own five-year series exists, stated as such [cov_publish comps, S0].

challenges.challenge: The +6.2% expected return is manufactured by the one-year 14.6% COE roll: on the marks, the parts are 4,589, 8.2% BELOW the 5,000 price, and the report concedes no dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. It also concedes in section 5 that the tabulated bear understates operating downside by Rp280-300/share while keeping 30% weight. The HOLD survives at a 40% discount (-8%), but the disclosed probability-weighted return is not the return a holder faces today.
challenges.answer: Accepted: un-rolled return disclosed as about minus three per cent, and with the operating-bear range inside the bear the weighted rolled return falls to about zero and un-rolled to about minus five; HOLD holds in both and the text says the cushion is the dividend and the discount, not the marks [S0, S15].

challenges.challenge: The property block is marked at Rp5,898bn by applying MMLP's 0.2275x market-to-assets ratio - a logistics/warehouse REIT multiple - to Menara Astra's Rp20,000bn of CBD office and warehouse assets, leaving about Rp20tn of the Others column's Rp58tn book equity outside the marks on an unsourced basis. The report calls the result a 'floor' but gives no Menara book equity, cap rate or appraised value; the card requires omitted assets at a sourced floor.
challenges.answer: Accepted: disclosed that 0.2275x is MMLP warehouse/logistics market-to-assets applied to CBD office, and quantified the markdown - Rp15,450bn of Menara assets outside the marks, about Rp253 per share after the discount [S15, S27].

challenges.challenge: The base's own -4.0% FY2027E share change implies the authorised Rp8tn buyback completes at about 5,000 against NAV of 7,060; at that 29% discount each retirement accretes NAV, roughly Rp85/share. The SOTP divides by the 30 September count of 39,687.6m and never carries that accretion, so the base assumes the buyback in the EPS/DPS lines and omits it from the parts.
challenges.answer: Accepted: stated that the SOTP divides by the 30 September count, pre-buyback, with the cash deducted through parent net debt and the retirement accretion of roughly Rp85 per share not credited [S15, S0].

challenges.challenge: Three figures for the same block's multiple are in circulation: 11.1961x on the 9M fact, 8.3971x annualised, '11.20x' in the bear narrative and '10.89x' in the bull narrative - one is wrong or stale. The report also uses S20's 31.2% October yoy while S33 says 'sekitar 10 persen' (81,482/62,090 = 31.2%, so S33 is wrong) without a note, and the bridge still shows 63,049 against the filed 64,925 [F100].

challenges.answer: One figure now, Rp420 per share, in the bear note and in section 5, with the 280-300 line deleted. It is priced at the bear 30% weight outside the table because the holdco_sotp engine holds each listed stake at the 6 November close and cannot reprice a mark inside a holding [S15, S0]; the all-in weighted value is about Rp4,568 and the return about minus 0.6%, both disclosed in the summary, section 4 and section 5. The published target of Rp4,694 and 1.9% are stated as excluding it, and the rating stays HOLD.
